if you’re a trader you have no idea how op adding episodic memory is to your agent.

what is this and why is it over powered?

the best traders in the world will attribute success to journalling their trades.

well that same journalling will let you create episodic memory which may well turn you from a shit trader who never learns his lessons into best trader you can become.

when you journal you should be recording:

> what did i expect the market to do?
> what actually happened?
> what was my directional bias?
> what setup did i take?
> why did i enter?
> where was my invalidation?
> how much did i risk?
> how did i size / scale the trade?
> what was my emotional state?
> did i feel fomo, fear, greed, boredom or complacency?
> did i actually follow my plan?
> why did i exit?
> what was the result?
> what did i do well?
> what did i fuck up?
> what lesson should i remember next time?

this will let you create episodic memory.

you can now tell your agent in the future:

> find every trade where i used this setup before
> show me how often it worked
> show me my average return
> show me the market conditions where it worked best
> show me the conditions where it failed
> show me the mistakes i normally make with this setup
> show me how my emotional state affected my execution
> show me similar losing trades and what went wrong
> show me similar winning trades and what i did right

and now when you go to make a trade and you journal:

> current market conditions
> directional bias
> setup
> entry
> invalidation
> risk
> sizing
> catalyst
> expected outcome
> emotional state

your agent can compare it against every similar trade you have taken before.

it can tell you the exact success rate you had with this exact setup.

it can tell you your average R.

it can tell you when the setup normally works.

it can tell you when it normally fails.

it can tell you the mistakes you repeatedly make.

it can even tell you:

“you have taken this setup 14 times before.

9 were winners.

your average return was +1.7R.

but when you entered before confirmation you lost 4 out of 5 times.”

now your agent is not just analysing the market.

it is analysing your own trading history.

every trade becomes another memory.

every mistake becomes something it can retrieve.

every successful setup becomes something it can compare against.

the more journalling the more episodic memory. the more episodic memory the more wins.

okay, I’m actually going to share a @bot with you guys soon so you can steal this.

The current barrier to greater AI diffusion isn’t model capability. In my eyes, the barrier is three things (in order):

1. Most people don’t understand what AI can do
2. They need to fundamentally think differently about their life and work
3. Human preference. Even if AI can do the thing, people still want to do it (like shopping)

Each layer is a more rigid barrier. First, someone must be motivated to understand. 

Then, they have to build a habit of flipping their thinking to a more AI-forward way. They need to consider how they would deconstruct and assign out work as if they were a manager. They need to understand abstract capabilities and apply them to their own use cases, or understand what previous use cases were uneconomical that are now available. 

Then they need to want to assign that task out to AI in the first place

All of this leads me to believe that we are still incredibly early. It will take 3-5 years for the middle of the curve to even understand today’s AI capabilities and change their mindset to put this technology to work on their behalf. And by then we will be much more advanced. 

The technological capability isn’t the blocker. It’s our understanding, creativity, and preferences that will determine the pace of diffusion

so ya hi, a few things.

First I don't want to belittle because you clearly put a lot of effort into this, great work.

But feel free to ask my anything in DMs, I'm an open book.

I'm very open about my addresses: any quit.<whatever>.eth address is most likely me, and unfuhquittable.eth is my primary wallet (holds my punk/ape etc).

osnipe and fwap are run entirely by me which is why they're linked to eachother (and me) onchain. They are me.

I use @limitbreak  to enforce transfer restrictions on any/every token I can and always recommend others do the same, because it's good tech. List 13 is owned by osnipe.eth and is my blanket list that has everything I need whitelisted (shadows bridge, nftstrategy contracts, autosniper contract, etc). It's easier than trying to manage several lists at once. It's also not limitbreak managed, it's 0xquit managed. Creating a list is permissionless.

I use @GuardianAudits any time I can afford to because they are the best/most thorough auditors I know, they're also my first recommendation any time somebody asks me to refer them to an auditor (if I'm not auditing myself).

@imjameshall built our internal Otherside marketplace on PaymentProcessor because again, it's good tech. We obviously did not know that it had this bug (and neither did anybody else for the past 2 years).

I was introduced to @Rhynotic after we found a bug in the original PunkStrategy and started a groupchat to remediate. Have since audited several of his projects including FWA.

I am connected to @0xjustadev and other DN404 contributors because when I wanted to build DN404 they were the best devs I knew (all the contributors you listed are goated).

If you keep digging you'll probably find I have my hand in just about every piece of the NFT space in some way - either as a dev, auditor, collector, or participant. Turns out I just like NFTs.

Hope that clears things up but let me know if you have any other questions 👍
